messages.content: I need to work out Atlanta for September 14 and 15. The district review starts Monday at 1:30 p.m. in Midtown, and Tuesday I have a restaurant visit north of downtown from 9:00 to 11:00. Compare flying Sunday evening versus Monday morning, then an early or evening flight home Tuesday. Don't book anything yet.

I'll compare nonstop round trips from Chicago O'Hare to Atlanta. What is the Monday address, and where is Tuesday's restaurant? Those locations will determine whether the tighter flights are realistic.
Monday is at 1100 Peachtree Street NE. Tuesday is in Roswell near Holcomb Bridge Road and Alpharetta Highway.

The useful outbound nonstops are Sunday, September 13, departing ORD at 7:10 p.m. and arriving ATL at 10:14 p.m., or Monday, September 14, departing at 8:10 a.m. and arriving at 11:15 a.m. Both are main-cabin fares. From ATL to 1100 Peachtree, allow roughly 25-50 minutes by car midday, plus pickup time. MARTA to Midtown takes about 30 minutes, followed by a short walk.
So the Monday flight is viable, but not with much room for a serious delay.

Correct. A normal arrival should put you at the review around noon to 12:20 p.m., leaving 70-90 minutes. A 45-minute flight or baggage delay would consume most of that margin. Sunday adds a hotel night but removes the same-day flight risk.
What do the Tuesday returns look like after Roswell?

The early nonstop leaves ATL at 1:40 p.m. and arrives ORD at 2:55 p.m. The evening nonstop leaves at 6:30 p.m. and arrives at 7:45 p.m. After an 11:00 a.m. finish in Roswell, the airport drive is typically 45-70 minutes before rental-car return or terminal access. The 1:40 departure would leave little tolerance for a late meeting or traffic; the 6:30 departure provides several hours.
Give me the totals for all four combinations. Same cabin and include the standard carry-on.

Current round-trip totals are: Sunday evening out and Tuesday early back, $412; Sunday evening out and Tuesday evening back, $438; Monday morning out and Tuesday early back, $389; Monday morning out and Tuesday evening back, $416. Each is nonstop in main cabin with one standard carry-on. Checked baggage and seat-selection charges are not included.
The early return doesn't make sense. Between the other two, does Sunday buy me anything besides avoiding the Monday flight risk?

It also lets you start Monday near Midtown without carrying luggage into the review. The tradeoff is one additional hotel night and $22 more airfare. With the Monday flight, you would need either an early bag drop at the hotel or luggage storage near the meeting. Ground cost from ATL is similar either way, though Sunday-night rideshare traffic may be lighter.

Use Monday morning out and Tuesday evening back for the hotel search. I want the lodging comparison to account for Monday bag storage, the review, Tuesday's Roswell drive, and getting back to ATL. Still no purchase.

Selected for planning only: Monday, September 14, ORD-ATL nonstop, 8:10-11:15 a.m.; Tuesday, September 15, ATL-ORD nonstop, 6:30-7:45 p.m.; $416 round trip in main cabin with a carry-on. Monday's review is at 1:30 p.m. at 1100 Peachtree Street NE, with an estimated 25-50-minute airport transfer and about 70-90 minutes of normal-arrival margin. Tuesday's Roswell visit runs 9:00-11:00 a.m.; Roswell to ATL is approximately 45-70 minutes, giving ample time for the evening flight. I'll use early luggage storage, Midtown access, the Roswell drive, airport-return timing, and the $416 airfare in the hotel and ground-transportation comparison. Nothing has been purchased.
